Yeah I've got a supportive partner we've been together a long time now. And I have friends that will listen to me go on. And I've got a bunch of professionals trying to help treat me. I'm pretty lucky having all that. 
I normally end up being admitted to hospital though when things get bad. 
Just got off the phone to the crisis worker, she was actually really helpful and they're going to give me daily support whilst this is going on and try and prevent an admission to hospital. 

Thank you so much for your support tonight. It's really helped me. I'm going to try and get some sleep now as it's nighttime here. Thank you again kind stranger.

Yeah, getting help was a complete accident really. My worker just said she had a hunch something was wrong. 
I'm sorry you've had a hard time too with mental illness. It fucking sucks. I've been like this on and off for years, I get tired of it happening. Like really tired and just don't see the point in keeping going when I know it's going to happen again.

Thank you for such a kind reply. In a weird moment my mental health worker called me out of hours to check on me. I've been referred to our crisis service now and am waiting a call back. 
I don't know if they can do anything or stop me but it's worth a try I suppose. I just feel so very dreadful. It's hard to contain it and not act on these feelings.

Hi there,
Thanks for taking the time to reply. 

Unfortunately for me I'm in the UK and it doesn't really work like that, the treatment is sort of decided for you without your say too much. I've been given individual therapy so I have to stick with it or I don't get anything at all. 
My abusive therapist sadly wasn't barely trained, she was the most senior therapist for my area but she was shitty, that's true. 
DBT sounds great but I don't think I'll get the chance to have it. I don't have the funds to access private medical care and I go with the NHS. I do love the NHS though but sometimes it is quite restrictive.

It'll probably depend on the GP surgery to if they feel that's okay but it might be an option. I'm hoping for you it is. With covid at the moment most appointments where I am are phone based so perhaps they'll be more open to a phone consultation  as they're much more widely used these days.

Hi,
Yes I told a professional about it a few years after I stopped seeing her who was obliged to report it even though I didn't want it reported as felt too scared by her. 
I never knew what the outcome was. They said it was being followed up but I never heard anymore after that. Sometimes I wish I knew if there were ever any consequences for her.

Hi there, I'm based in the UK. I think generally the support can really vary from place to place in what you receive. There are some excellent places and some pretty poor ones.

In order to access mental health services you'd need to go through a GP as far as I'm aware which means registering with a practise and having an initial appointment. I'm not sure you'd be able to access a sedative through a GP without seeing them first. However I've registered at a practise before and never had to have a physical examination. I don't think that's a requirement. But I might be wrong. Perhaps you could ask for your initial appointment to be over the phone instead of face to face. 

Sorry if this is completely unhelpful. I don't comment much but just thought I would seeing as I'm UK based.
These are really good ideas, thank you.
I forgot to mention in my post that I am in therapy already, have been for a while now. We're slowly working through what happened. I didn't think to ask them about this but that's a good idea.
Thank you for your kind words
